body:
@dchard 

```
5.5.2 Conditions for sending TEID=0 in GTPv2-C header
If a peer's TEID is not available, the TEID field still shall be present in the header and its value shall be
set to "0" in the following messages:
 -Create Session Request message on S2a/S2b/S5/S8
 -Create Session Request message on S4/S11, if for a given UE, the SGSN/MME has not yet obtained
  the Control TEID of the SGW.
 ...
 ...
```

As per 3GPP TS 29.274, Section 5.5.2, the TEID field must always be present in the GTPv2-C header. If a TEID value is not available, the field should still be included and set to "0". This requirement applies to Create Session Request messages on interfaces such as S2a, S2b, S5, and S8, as well as on S4 and S11 under specific conditions.

If the Create Session Request message from your 3rd Party SGW does not include the TEID field, it is not compliant with 3GPP specifications. I recommend verifying whether the TEID field is missing or improperly formatted in the message sent by your SGW.

Could you please confirm this information and provide additional details, such as a packet capture of the Create Session Request message? This will help us analyze the issue further and provide more specific guidance.

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

@acetcom 

Yes, I found exactly the same part, but I just read it as the TEID flag should be present and should be set to 0 (which it is). But if I read it more carefully, the spec uses the "flag" and "field" terminology half a page earlier:

Bit 4 represents a "T" flag, which indicates if TEID field is present in the GTP-C header or not. If the "T" flag is
set to 0, then the TEID field shall not be present in the GTP-C header. If the "T" flag is set to 1, then the TEID
field shall immediately follow the Length field, in octets 5 to 8.

So you are correct: my 3rd party SGW does include the TEID=0 flag, but it does not include the TEID=0x00000000 field. Therefor the 3rd party SGW is at fault here.

Sorry for the noise, I am closing this as the situation is rather clear.
